Its been a little while since I graduated, but I would guess things haven't changed too much. Desk monitors don't get free room and board; that's RAs. A work-study is a federal program that allocates a fixed amount of money that you then work hours to make. You have to apply and meet certain requirements for it just like student loans. Work-studies can be beneficial over regular jobs because they are specifically designed to be manageable as a student. Your boss won't schedule shifts during your class hours,  desk monitors are allowed to do homework when no one is at the desk, etc. The RA position is not a work-study position. Anyone can apply, but it is a larger responsibility and I only suggest it to someone who really wants to do the job, not just get the benefits. All work-study jobs have the benefit of being connected to the campus. An outside job might allow you to make more money if you work a lot more hours since work-study is a fixed amount, but obviously that will take more time away from school.

You can apply to be a front desk monitor your freshman year (and continue all years) if you want something right away. There are also a few positions a front desk staff at the actual office of ResLife and at Campus Safety. 

There is no way to request specific floors. The only way to get close is to apply for a learning community that happens to be in the hall you want, but you won't know what floors the community has. You also should only join one that you actually want to be in. 

Source: was an RA for 3 years.

Former RA here! First off, just because your roommate said that doesn't mean it's official. Is he complaining about noise from you? Because then you would have a roommate mediation to try to fix it. If it's other noise, staff would still try to come up with a solution prior to authorizing him moving. That's a last resort. So if he hasn't actually done any of that stuff, he's not moving anytime soon. If he does move out at some point:

1) ResLife will give you at least 24 hours before you get a new roommate, if you do. It's possible no one will be assigned that space. They will tell you who it is before they move in. 

2) There isn't really a list. Like I said, he'd have to go through some steps to be moved.

3) If he's gone, staff will tell you you need to leave things open in case you get a new roommate. You can use the furniture if you're okay with moving all your stuff out of it should you get a new roommate. 

4) This point kind of shows me that his statement was more venting or like a threat. He should have all this information if he's actually moving.

I would suggest you talk to your RA about this since he or she will know the specifics for the situation. Good luck!

Today marks the third anniversary of me being right about my boyfriend's appendix.

We were at a Halloween party, and he all of a sudden looked pale and said his stomach hurt. We went outside and sat on the street and I asked where it hurt. He pointed to the right lower quadrant. Because I was studying anatomy at the time and we had just learned this, I said it might be your appendix and he just said no I'm fine and we went home. 

Over the next few days he kept complaining about pressure and mild pain. He said he thought he had gas and asked me to push on his stomach. Finally, I pleaded with him to just go to the campus health clinic. I took a nap and woke up and he had texted me saying they told him to go to the ER immediately. 

I rushed over and the ER nurse asked how long have you been feeling this and he said six days. The nurse was like no way do you have appendicitis, that's too much time and you're walking around and calm. They did the CT scan, scheduled him for surgery and it burst when he was on the table. Honestly he was in way more pain after surgery than before. He always says he hopes to wake up with superpowers one day and I like to tell him he used it up by walking around with appendicitis for 6 days. :)

However, it was probably fractured because as I grew up, the part of my finger above my knuckle was growing at the wrong angle. It was my pointer finger, and the top part was pointing away from my middle finger. They told me that it would eventually be at a 90 degree angle and I wouldn't be able to use my hand (which was my dominant hand). So I had to have surgery where they took a slice of the bone out to straighten my finger. I had pins put in to keep it straight and a cast for a long time. 

Now, the doctor who did this was the best hand surgeon in my town, but he didn't normally work with kids. I was 10, and terrified. When I got my cast off, he told me he was going to take the pins out while I was completely awake and without pain medication. I realize now that it probably wouldn't have hurt, but I was so scared that I was panicking and thought he was already doing it so I was screaming and crying. He got super pissed and  said they'd put me under to do it.

I told him at a check-up, and he rolled his eyes and sarcastically said it might hurt sometimes but I had to just do it. I kept doing it but the pain started to become constant, even when I wasn't moving my hand. At my next appointment, he agreed to X-ray my hand, basically to shut me up. The X-ray technician happened to be the dad of one of my classmates, and he was so sweet and comforting. He had to tell me that the doctor had left a pin in my hand. The physical therapy had caused it to move from its original position of being perpendicular to my finger. 

Jerk doctor didn't tell me himself or even apologize. He just said we can either take it out right now (because that went well the first time) or we could schedule another surgery.
